explanation: pthread_mutexattr_getpshared is a function in the POSIX threads library that retrieves the process-shared attribute from a mutex attribute object. It is used to determine whether a mutex can be shared between processes, which is essential for managing synchronization in multithreaded or multiprocess applications to prevent race conditions and ensure proper resource sharing.
example_explanation: This program initializes a mutex attribute object using pthread_mutexattr_init, then calls pthread_mutexattr_getpshared to retrieve and store the process-shared attribute in the pshared variable. It prints the value if the call succeeds, demonstrating how the function queries the attribute before destroying the object, focusing solely on this concept.
